question: The bakery made 95 muffins. They will be packed in boxes with 5 muffins in each box. If there are only 10 available boxes, how many boxes do they still need to pack all the muffins?

student_prefix.content: The bakery made 95 muffins. They will be packed in boxes with 5 muffins in each box. If there are only 10 available boxes, how many boxes do they still need to pack all the muffins?

Given:
- Total muffins: 95
- Muffins per box: 5
- Available boxes: 10

First, calculate the total number of boxes needed to pack all the muffins:
\[ \text{Total boxes needed} = \frac{95 \text{ muffins}}{5 \text{ muffins/box}} = 19 \text{ boxes} \]

Next, determine how many more boxes are needed by subtracting the available boxes from the total boxes needed:
\[ \text{Additional boxes needed} = 19 \text{ boxes} - 10 \text{ boxes} = 9 \text{ boxes} \]

FINAL: 9
